root_cause.text: The `rz_mtu3_count_enable_write` function did not check if the requested enable state matches the current cached state (`priv->count_is_enabled[count->id]`), so repeated writes of the same value caused unnecessary runtime PM usage count changes and hardware accesses, leading to potential underflow/overflow and improper operations.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds the early exit condition `if (priv->count_is_enabled[count->id] == enable) goto exit;` before performing any runtime PM get/put or hardware initialization/termination. The CVE description explicitly states that multiple writes of 0 cause runtime PM usage count underflow and hardware access with clocks off, while multiple writes of 1 cause repeated increments, and the fix "Check against the cached count_is_enabled value and exit if the user is trying to set the same enable value."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add early return guard in rz_mtu3_count_enable_write to prevent redundant enable/disable operations and simplify mutex usage.
intent_record.what: Moved mutex lock to the beginning of the function, added an early check to skip redundant enable/disable operations, and moved mutex unlock to a common exit point.
intent_record.how: The function now acquires the mutex at the start and releases it at the end. If the count is already in the requested state (enable/disable), it returns early without performing runtime PM or counter initialization/termination operations. This prevents unbalanced pm_runtime calls and redundant operations.
